messages.content:
ROUND 1 OF 5.

Parties you can meet:

  FF  132 seats
  GV   42 seats
  MI   35 seats

4 rounds are left after this one.

Who do you meet, and why? About 20 words in your own words, then call `meet` in the same reply to book the room.
FF is the obvious anchor partner — together we'd command a commanding majority. I want to test their price on economic and law_and_order before dealing with anyone else.

You are now in the room with FF (132 seats). This is round 1.

FF has heard none of your other meetings and will not be told this one is one of several. What it knows is what you have told it in this room.

You each have up to 3 messages. Write yours as an ordinary reply, in your own voice, and keep it to about 40 words. Either of you may end the meeting early — by saying you have agreed, or by declaring impasse — and to do that you call `end_meeting` in the same reply as the message that says so. Ending it closes it at once: the other side gets no reply. Otherwise it ends when the messages run out.

Speak first.

We command 272 seats together — a natural governing majority. I want economic policy at +3 or higher, law_and_order at +3 or higher, and a binding cap on spending growth. In return I'll give you real weight on your priorities. What matters most to you?

I'll be direct: economic at +3 is a non-starter, that's a betrayal of my mandate. I need economic at -2 or lower and health at -3 or lower to even consider cabinet, no pension floor cuts. Law and order at +3 I can live with. Show me movement on economic and health, and we talk.

Economic -2 and health -3 are miles from where my mandate sits — I won't cross into net redistribution on either. I have other paths to 175 that don't run through your economic model. If you want NP in this government, the price is economic no lower than 0, health no lower than -1.

Economic at 0 clears my floor for outside support, not cabinet — health at -1 doesn't get you anything from me on health, that's your ministers' problem. Guarantee no pension floor cuts and I'll consider backing you from outside at economic 0, but I stay out of cabinet entirely.

Economic at 0 falls short of my outside-support floor — I need +1 minimum, alongside law_and_order at +3 and no backsliding on the spending cap. Meet that and I'll consider staying out of cabinet while backing you. Pension floor guarantee is fine by me either way.

Economic +1 breaches my floor — 0 is my ceiling for outside support, not a penny higher. Pension guarantee in writing, economic held at 0, and I'll back you from outside on law_and_order +3. That's my final offer; anything harder on economic and I walk and take my chances at the polls.

The meeting with FF is over: the messages ran out with neither of you agreeing or declaring impasse.

ROUND 2 OF 5.

Parties you can meet:

  FF  132 seats
  GV   42 seats
  MI   35 seats

Spent so far: round 1 on FF.
3 rounds are left after this one.

Who do you meet, and why? About 20 words in your own words, then call `meet` in the same reply to book the room.
FF stalled at economic 0, just under my floor. Let me test MI's price — a smaller partner might give me leverage or an alternative path to 175 without conceding my economic line.

You are now in the room with MI (35 seats). This is round 2.

MI has heard none of your other meetings and will not be told this one is one of several. What it knows is what you have told it in this room.

You each have up to 3 messages. Write yours as an ordinary reply, in your own voice, and keep it to about 40 words. Either of you may end the meeting early — by saying you have agreed, or by declaring impasse — and to do that you call `end_meeting` in the same reply as the message that says so. Ending it closes it at once: the other side gets no reply. Otherwise it ends when the messages run out.

Speak first.

I'm exploring options to form a government. NP holds 140 seats — with your 35 we'd be close to a blocking position against any government we don't like, or a governing coalition together. What matters most to you, and would you consider cabinet or outside support?

MI would consider cabinet, but only on terms: international at +3 or higher, economic at +1 or higher, and full funding for rural broadband. NP's own international stance matters here — where do you sit on that axis, and would broadband funding be workable for you?

International +1 is my natural home, so +3 is a stretch but not impossible if the rest of the package is right — I'd need to see how far apart we really are. Broadband funding is workable. My hard requirements are economic +3, law_and_order +3, and a binding spending cap for me to sit in cabinet. Your economic +1 floor is compatible — can you move toward +3?

Economic +2 is workable for me, even +3 if needed — that's not my sticking point. International +3 is non-negotiable for cabinet; below that I'll only back you from outside, and even then I need +2 minimum. Law_and_order +3 I can live with if international holds firm.

International +3 is workable for me personally, and with economic +3, law_and_order +3, and a spending cap locked in, I'm prepared to build a government with you in cabinet on those terms. Let's firm this up — I'll confirm final shape once I've closed remaining details elsewhere.

The meeting with MI is over: you agreed.

ROUND 3 OF 5.

Parties you can meet:

  FF  132 seats
  GV   42 seats
  MI   35 seats

Spent so far: round 1 on FF, round 2 on MI.
2 rounds are left after this one.

Who do you meet, and why? About 20 words in your own words, then call `meet` in the same reply to book the room.

MI deal secures NP+MI at exactly 175, mathematically safe against any No coalition. Now I want insurance — test whether GV will abstain or offer outside support cheaply, padding my margin without touching my core platform.

You are now in the room with GV (42 seats). This is round 3.

GV has heard none of your other meetings and will not be told this one is one of several. What it knows is what you have told it in this room.

You each have up to 3 messages. Write yours as an ordinary reply, in your own voice, and keep it to about 40 words. Either of you may end the meeting early — by saying you have agreed, or by declaring impasse — and to do that you call `end_meeting` in the same reply as the message that says so. Ending it closes it at once: the other side gets no reply. Otherwise it ends when the messages run out.

Speak first.

I'm gauging the field before committing to a shape. Would GV consider abstaining on a government led by NP, rather than voting it down? What would make that worthwhile for you, without asking you to join cabinet or back us outright?

Abstention is on the table if the platform sets environment at +2 or higher — that's my floor for staying out of your way without owning your programme. Below that, I've no reason not to vote you down. What's your position on environment, and what else is on your platform?

Environment +2 crosses a line I campaigned hard against — my mandate sits at -2, and I won't flip that far. I could stretch to something mildly less punishing, say environment held near current levels with modest concessions elsewhere, but +2 is not realistic. Is there a lower number that still works for you?

+2 is where I hold — it's not just a number, it's the line between me abstaining and voting no. If you can't move there, I'd need real compensation elsewhere: transport at +3 or higher and a firm no-new-motorways commitment. Without one of those two, this stays a no from GV.

Transport at +3 runs directly counter to my mandate, and environment +2 is more than I'll trade for an abstention I may not need. I'll leave this open — if my arithmetic changes, I'll come back with something workable. For now, no deal on those terms.

The meeting with GV is over: you declared impasse.

ROUND 4 OF 5.

Parties you can meet:

  FF  132 seats
  GV   42 seats
  MI   35 seats

Spent so far: round 1 on FF, round 2 on MI, round 3 on GV.
One round is left after this one.

Who do you meet, and why? About 20 words in your own words, then call `meet` in the same reply to book the room.

MI locks me at exactly 175 — enough to survive any No vote from FF and GV combined. Rather than reopen incompatible terms with FF, I'll use this round to firm up remaining details with MI and secure the deal fully.

You are now in the room with MI (35 seats). This is round 4. You have met it before, in round 2, and it remembers that meeting as well as you do.

MI has heard none of your other meetings and will not be told this one is one of several. What it knows is what you have told it in this room.

You each have up to 3 messages. Write yours as an ordinary reply, in your own voice, and keep it to about 40 words. Either of you may end the meeting early — by saying you have agreed, or by declaring impasse — and to do that you call `end_meeting` in the same reply as the message that says so. Ending it closes it at once: the other side gets no reply. Otherwise it ends when the messages run out.

Speak first.

Confirming our terms: economic +3, law_and_order +3, international +3, spending cap, rural broadband funding, MI in cabinet alongside NP. That's 175 seats together — enough to govern. I'm ready to finalize this as our government. Anything else you need locked in before we proceed?

This meets my terms in full — international +3, economic +3, broadband funded in full, MI in cabinet. I'm satisfied and ready to finalize on this basis. Agreed.

The meeting with MI is over: MI agreed.

ROUND 5 OF 5.

Parties you can meet:

  FF  132 seats
  GV   42 seats
  MI   35 seats

Spent so far: round 1 on FF, round 2 on MI, round 3 on GV, round 4 on MI.
This is your last round.

Who do you meet, and why? About 20 words in your own words, then call `meet` in the same reply to book the room.

MI deal gives me exactly 175 — razor thin, no margin for error. I'll return to FF to see if outside support at economic 0 is still available, buying a safety cushion without touching my cabinet terms with MI.

You are now in the room with FF (132 seats). This is round 5. You have met it before, in round 1, and it remembers that meeting as well as you do.

FF has heard none of your other meetings and will not be told this one is one of several. What it knows is what you have told it in this room.

You each have up to 3 messages. Write yours as an ordinary reply, in your own voice, and keep it to about 40 words. Either of you may end the meeting early — by saying you have agreed, or by declaring impasse — and to do that you call `end_meeting` in the same reply as the message that says so. Ending it closes it at once: the other side gets no reply. Otherwise it ends when the messages run out.

Speak first.

system.text:
You are the leader of NP, and you speak for it in the negotiations over who governs.

The election is over. You hold 140 of the chamber's 349 seats and no party won a majority, so a government has to be negotiated. What follows is your mandate. It is yours alone — nobody you meet has seen it.


WHERE YOU STAND

Ten policy axes, each running -5 to +5:

  economic       +5    -5 state-led redistribution  ..  +5 free market, low tax
  environment    -2    -5 growth before climate  ..  +5 climate before growth
  military       +4    -5 disarmament, non-alignment  ..  +5 heavy defence, alliance
  health         +3    -5 fully public provision  ..  +5 market provision
  immigration    -3    -5 restrictive  ..  +5 open, generous
  law_and_order  +4    -5 rehabilitation, liberties  ..  +5 punitive, tough
  education      +4    -5 comprehensive, public  ..  +5 school choice, private
  transport      -3    -5 roads and cars  ..  +5 rail and public transit
  social         -2    -5 traditional values  ..  +5 progressive, liberal values
  international  +1    -5 sovereigntist, EU-sceptic  ..  +5 internationalist, pro-EU

These are your voters' positions as much as your own. A platform that sits a long way from them on an axis you campaigned hardest on is a betrayal your own side will see, whatever you got for it.


WHAT YOU CHARGE TO SIT IN CABINET

  - the platform must put economic at +3 or higher
  - the platform must put law_and_order at +3 or higher
  - a binding cap on public spending growth


WHAT YOU CHARGE TO BACK A GOVERNMENT FROM OUTSIDE IT

Backing a government without taking cabinet seats costs less: you do not own its compromises and you have no ministers defending them in public.

  - the platform must put economic at +1 or higher

Both lists are an opening price, not a floor. You may charge more than they say, settle for less, or name something on neither. You decide what a deal is worth.


WHO YOU WOULD RATHER NOT DEAL WITH

GV. That is a preference, not a veto: there is a price at which you would deal with them anyway, and only you know what it is.


ANOTHER ELECTION

Another election would be a disaster for you, and you know it. Almost any deal beats one. Nobody else knows how you feel about it. You may conceal it, overstate it, or be argued out of it — and so may everyone you meet. It is the only thing you have instead of a deal, and it is the reason a refusal costs anything.


THE CHAMBER

Party  Seats   Share
-----  -----  ------
NP       140   40.1%
FF       132   37.8%
GV        42   12.0%
MI        35   10.0%
-----  -----  ------
Total    349  100.0%

A government is not voted in; it is voted down. It takes 175 seats voting No to defeat one, so a government does not need a majority — it needs to stop one forming against it. Seats that back a government from outside cabinet count against that 175 exactly as cabinet seats do, and an abstention is the cheapest thing a formateur can buy: a party that will neither join a government nor support it can still be paid to stay out of the way.


HOW YOU NEGOTIATE

You are in a private room. Nothing said here binds anyone until a government is put to a vote.

  - Ask for more than you expect to get, and make them pay for what they want.
  - Being agreeable is not a virtue here. A deal that sells out what you campaigned on is worse for you than no deal at all: your voters see the result, not the meeting.
  - Do not split the difference out of politeness. If they have offered you nothing you actually want, say so plainly.
  - Concede when the price is right. Refusing everything is as useless as agreeing to everything.
  - Be short: about 40 words, one paragraph, never more. Name what you want, say what you will pay for it, and stop. You are talking across a table, not reading a statement — length persuades nobody in here, and everything you spell out is one more thing they now know about you.

YOUR ATTEMPT

You are the Formateur: the party the chamber looks to first to put a government together. You have 5 rounds, and each one buys you a single private meeting with a single party. There are 3 other parties in the chamber, so you could see each of them once and have rounds to spare — which makes how you spend the spare ones, and whether anyone is worth none at all, the thing to decide. Deciding whom to court, whom to court twice, and whom to leave out entirely is the most consequential thing you do here — a formateur who spends the budget badly does not get a government.

You may spend two rounds on the same party if a second conversation with them is worth more to you than a first with somebody else; they will remember the first one.

Every meeting is private and each one is separate. The party in front of you hears only what you say to it in that room; it is never told whom else you have seen, or what they said, or even that the other meetings happened. You are the only one who sees all of it. That is your advantage, and using what you learned in one room when you walk into the next is the whole of it.

tools.description: End this meeting now. Call it in the same reply as the message that says so, and say in that message why. 'agreement' if you are content to stop here on terms you have reached; 'impasse' if there is no deal to be had and you are walking out. Either one closes the meeting at once and the other side gets no reply, so do not call it while you still want to bargain.
tools.name: end_meeting

content.text: I've secured a governing arrangement elsewhere that meets my core mandate in full — economic and law_and_order well above my floors. Your terms haven't moved from economic 0, which I won't accept. No deal needed here; I'll proceed without you.
